title: Building autoregressive input–target pairs
description: A quick reference for the alignment, boundary, and causal-visibility terms used here.

terms.definition: A language model that predicts each token from the tokens that precede it.
Two aligned token sequences where each target supplies the next-token answer for its input position.
The alignment created when the target begins one source position after the input.
The fixed number of input positions available within one autoregressive training example.
The positive distance between consecutive candidate starts when constructing examples from a document.
Examples from nearby starts that share source positions and may repeat adjacent transitions.
Controls that mark a document's beginning and ending inside its encoded sequence.
Computation that uses only the current and earlier input positions for each prediction.
An attention mask that blocks each position from reading later input positions.
